text:
Support Bot: Automated alert from rate_limit-service — sudden spike of 429s for customer cust-1234 across eu-west-1 between 2026-03-15T10:20Z and 10:28Z. rate_limit.denied = 450 (8m). Opening thread for triage.

Maria T: Lina (CS) just forwarded a customer screenshot — they're seeing lots of 429s and say billing jumped unexpectedly. They attached a response body showing Retry-After=10. Can someone pull logs and attribution? @SRE Oncall? :eyes:

Lina (CS): Customer repro steps (from them): they run a processing job that fan-outs requests to /v1/generate with concurrency=50 per worker, no backoff on 5xx, and they retried on 429 immediately. Happened right after a deploy of their worker yesterday. They included one raw response: 

```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Content-Type: application/json
Retry-After: 10
{
  "error": "rate_limit_exceeded",
  "retry_after": 10,
  "scope": "project",
  "message": "Tokens per minute exceeded for project"
}
```

Maria T: customer id is cust-1234, project p-9876. They want to know: why did quotas hit, why billing shows extra token charges (they claim retries doubled usage), and how to avoid in future.

Jamal R: First pass checklist: 1) grab request_ids and sample logs for the window (2026-03-15T10:15-10:30Z) 2) check per-route & per-model metrics 3) see if burst/queueing was happening on a shard. I'll start pulling logs.

Alex P: Quick grafana queries I ran: 

- rate_limit denied by customer: `sum(rate_limit_denied{customer_id="cust-1234"}) by (customer_id)`
- route-level denied: `sum(rate_limit_denied) by (route)` and `sum(route_request_count) by (route)`

I see `/v1/generate` accounted for ~92% of denied tokens in that window. Model tag also shows `redwood-llama-13b` in most denied requests. Link to dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/limits/quotas?from=now-1h&to=now&var-customer=cust-1234

Alex P: From logs (sample):

```
2026-03-15T10:22:03Z request_id=rid-73a customer=cust-1234 route=/v1/generate model=redwood-llama-13b tokens=1024 result=429 reason=rate_limit_exceeded
2026-03-15T10:22:03Z request_id=rid-73b customer=cust-1234 route=/v1/generate model=redwood-llama-13b tokens=512 result=429 reason=rate_limit_exceeded
2026-03-15T10:22:04Z request_id=rid-73c customer=cust-1234 route=/v1/generate model=redwood-llama-13b tokens=1024 result=200 latency_ms=210
```

Alex P: Looks like a mix of allowed and denied — suggests bursty traffic, some succeeded, many hit the token bucket threshold. Also noticed the customer retried a lot: same request_id pattern with quick repeats in logs.

Lina (CS): Customer confirms their client retried instantly on 429 and on 5xx. They didn't implement exponential backoff or jitter. They also used the same API key across thousands of short-lived containers.

Jamal R: Attribution notes: we attribute throttling by these tags — customer_id, route, model, and token_bucket_id. For observability we should check: `rate_limit_denied/count by (customer_id,route,model,token_bucket)` and `token_usage/second by (customer_id)`. If a single customer consumes all burst capacity, it will look like quota exhaustion rather than system-wide overload.

SRE Oncall: For immediate mitigations: 
- Temporary: bump the burst_limit for cust-1234 by a controlled amount to get them unblocked while CS coordinates a client fix (note billing impact).
- Short-term: add server-side 429 smoothing — we can increase `burst_capacity` on the shard serving their traffic for 10 minutes.
- Long-term: alert & dashboard changes (see below).

SRE Oncall: Recommended alert rules to add: 
- `alert_rate_limit_ratio`: fire when `sum(rate_limit_denied{customer_id!=""}) by (customer_id, 5m) / sum(route_request_count) by (customer_id, 5m) > 0.02` for 3 mins. (This highlights customers whose requests are >2% being denied).
- `alert_burst_exhausted`: fire when `token_bucket_available < threshold` for a token_bucket serving >1k r/s.
- Add panels to per-customer dashboard: `rate_limit_denied`, `rate_limit_allowed`, `retry_attempts`, `avg_tokens_per_request`, `model_breakdown` (tags).

Maria T: Also we should include billing guardrails: if retries cause a billing spike, ability to flag a customer for a temporary invoice review or credit. Ping @billing to confirm if we can offer a one-time courtesy credit for the duplicate token usage while they fix retry logic.

Alex P: If we go the temporary bump route, do it this way (admin API call):

```
curl -X POST https://console.redwood.internal/internal/quotas \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"customer_id":"cust-1234","burst_limit":12000,"rate_limit_per_minute":300000,"note":"temporary bump 2026-03-15 - CS coordinated"}'
```
Make sure to tag change with `temp-bump-cust-1234` and set TTL in the console.

Jamal R: I'll collect the necessary artifacts for the ticket: list of `request_id`s, sample 429 bodies, time window, the grafana panels, and approximate extra tokens charged due to retries. Maria — can you ask the customer to share a HAR or capture of their client logs showing retry timings? That will confirm immediate retries.

Lina (CS): I'll ask them for the HAR and let them know recommended fixes: 1) implement exponential backoff with jitter, 2) respect Retry-After header, 3) reduce concurrency per API key or rotate keys per worker pool.

SRE Oncall: Longer-term observability improvements we should track in the backlog: 
- Per-customer request anomaly detection (spikes in concurrency / token-rate).
- Attribution panel that shows `throttled_tokens_by_route/model/customer` with clickable links to traces and logs.
- Add a `throttle_reason` tag to responses so dashboards can break down 429 by `reason=burst|rate|quota|model_limit`.

Maria T: For now CS asked for a one-hour temporary bump while they fix. Is that ok? Jamal, Alex — what are the risks?

Alex P: Risk is increased cost if they truly misuse. But if it's temporary and TTL is set, it's fine. Also recommend we set a throttling alert to auto-roll-back bump if abuse continues.

Jamal R: Agree. I'll prepare an evidence pack and tag SRE lead for approval. Billing, please hold on invoice adjustments until we know exact duplicated tokens due to retries.

Support Bot: Triage checklist (to close thread once done): [x] collect request_ids & logs, [x] pull grafana panels, [x] confirm retry behavior from customer, [ ] temporary quota bump (pending approval), [ ] billing review, [ ] create follow-up runbook item for per-customer throttling observability. Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/rate-limits (internal)

Maria T: thanks everyone — I'll update Lina and keep this thread in case customer responds with HAR. :thumbsup:

Lina (CS): Customer provided HAR and we can see immediate retries at ~200ms intervals. I've scheduled a call for 16:00 UTC to walk them through backoff changes.

SRE Oncall: Marking follow-ups: 1) create alert `alert_rate_limit_ratio` 2) add `throttle_reason` tag in responses 3) add per-customer dashboard variables. I'll file tickets and link back here.

Alex P: If anyone needs command snippets or queries, ping me and I'll drop them.

Support Bot: Thread closed for now — escalate to SRE oncall if the customer requests immediate capacity without the agreed TTL or if abuse suspected.
